title: Lifelong Embodied Navigation Learning
claim: Agents must continually learn a sequence of tasks across varied scenes and instruction styles while retaining earlier knowledge.
layout: 3 stacked horizontal bands, left-to-right task timeline arrow on top, dashed boxes
description: A wide figure with a task-timeline arrow across the top (Task 1 … Task t-1 … Task t). Below it are three stacked bands. The top dashed band, titled 'Uni-Walker lifelong learning in multi-instruction styles', shows three instruction-style cards linked by arrows: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN), Object Localization Navigation (OLN) and Dialogue Understanding Navigation (DUN). Each card has example user text and a 'Thinking' bubble. The middle band shows robot versions Uni-Walker V1, V2 and V3 as cartoon robots. Each robot has a thought bubble listing its skills (VLN, then VLN+OLN, then VLN+DUN+OLN) and stacked-layer icons. Each robot is next to a 3D indoor scan with a blue navigation path. The bottom band, 'lifelong learning in multi-navigation scenes', shows a row of scenes (Scene 1 to Scene t) linked by arrows. The blue-to-yellow gradient suggests time passing, and the red section titles draw the eye first.
caption: Illustration of the proposed lifelong embodied navigation learning (LENL) task. The proposed Uni-Walker is able to evolve and continually learn multiple new navigation tasks based on learned navigation knowledge, for developing universal embodied navigation. In lifelong learning, the sequential navigation tasks include multi-scenes and multi-instruction styles (VLN, OLN, DUN).
abstract: Embodied navigation agents powered by large language models have shown strong performance on individual tasks but struggle to continually acquire new navigation skills, which suffer from catastrophic forgetting. We formalize this challenge as lifelong embodied navigation learning (LENL), where an agent is required to adapt to a sequence of navigation tasks spanning multiple scenes and diverse user instruction styles, while retaining previously learned knowledge. To tackle this problem, we propose Uni-Walker, a lifelong embodied navigation framework that decouples navigation knowledge into task-shared and task-specific components with Decoder Extension LoRA (DE-LoRA). To learn the shared knowledge, we design a knowledge inheritance strategy and an experts co-activation strategy to facilitate shared knowledge transfer and refinement across multiple navigation tasks. To learn the specific knowledge, we propose an expert subspace orthogonality constraint together and a navigation-specific chain-of-thought reasoning mechanism to capture specific knowledge and enhance instruction-style understanding. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of Uni-Walker for building universal navigation agents with lifelong learning.
